inspiredBy.author: @everestchris6
inspiredBy.note: Remade from scratch in HyperFrames after an AI-made concept film for a roofing inspection brand; the scene order, the type system and the transitions follow it. The original's own fictional brand is replaced with a different one. The five photos were generated with the Claude Imagine MCP; the house, the roof cutaway, the turning view with pinned photos, the shingle tiles and the extruded mark are drawn live by a small orthographic 3D renderer into SVG, so they turn and come apart for real instead of being stills.

items.title: Kiteva / 瑞士网格排版
items.tags: 瑞士网格排版 International Typographic Style (Swiss Style) Use a column grid, baseline alignment, repeated spacing, asymmetric composition, and generous negative space. Set left-aligned sans-serif type with clear size hierarchy; use black and white with restrained accent colors and grid-aligned photography. Animate along layout axes and settle elements on shared alignment points without disrupting reading order.

A 120 px grid, 120 BPM, and 20 beats are optional starting parameters, not defining features.

items.title: Kiteva / 日式漫画
items.tags: 日式漫画 Manga Authored manga illustration with subject-specific storytelling: people, animals, creatures, monsters, objects, machines, environments or abstract subjects as required by the brief. Drawing quality must carry a still frame; generic icons, dashboard cards or a blanket dot filter are not substitutes for refined manga drawing.

items.title: Kiteva / 漫画制作剧场
items.tags: 漫画制作剧场 Manga Production Theatre A mostly black-and-white backstage manga in one continuous film set. Preserve white round-headed, faceless, short-bodied characters with pointed feet, bold ink outlines and halftone scenery. A persistent director speaks beside a shadowed presentation board while stage, camera, lighting, art and sound crew perform tasks supported by timed storyboard JSON. Backgrounds and boards travel right to left; crew make brief trips to work positions and return for reading holds. Use compact black name badges, readable rounded status labels and small board captions. Oval speech and thought balloons stay above the director, with extra headroom for thought circles. Use #F47B45 sparingly for playback progress, working-crew dots, brief dialogue-change underlines, equipment indicators and an optional opening-title accent. Keep the opening title optional and opening-only; never repeat title cards per scene. Default cast identity: whenever Manga Production Theatre is selected or named, use the established storyboard crew as its character reference without requiring the brief to repeat it. Figures have a large blank white circular head, a compact white cutout body with small side arm points and two pointed feet, a continuous bold black contour and no facial features, fingers or jointed skeletal limbs. Keep head/body proportions, outline weight and prop scale consistent across scenes; use short whole-figure tilts, turns and pose changes rather than substituting generic line-stick people, rounded capsule mascots or realistic humans. The director is slightly larger and remains the persistent narrator beside the board. Roles must be recognizable from their silhouettes and equipment as well as their readable badges: DIRECTOR with a clapperboard; STAGE CREW carrying a prop box; ART DEPT with an oversized pencil; LIGHTING with an adjustable lamp on a stand; SOUND wearing headphones and operating a small mixer; CAMERA with a twin-reel camera and tripod. Keep each figure attached to the same role and prop throughout the film. Show only crew with an actual task, preserving the role-specific action and idle rules; do not invent work just to fill the cast. Explicit user changes take precedence.

items.title: Kiteva / 磁带未来
items.tags: 磁带未来 Cassette Futurism Cassette Futurism: the 1970s–80s imagined spaceship and mission-control console, a hardware-first branch of Retrofuturism rather than cyberpunk, vaporwave or Y2K. Compose a modular dashboard of chunky charcoal and olive panels set into beige plastic cases with visible screws, seams, vents and black or white embossed labels, banded by restrained amber, orange and rust livery stripes. Recessed black CRT screens glow in ONE phosphor per screen — green #74FF9A or amber #FFB23E — with modest scanlines, soft glow, a screen-bounded vignette and seeded deterministic noise. Use monospace or pixel-like type from locally available system mono fonts: condensed uppercase panel labels such as NAV, PWR and SYS, numbers, timecodes and segmented readouts. Physical hardware carries the scene: cassette tape reels and transport, toggles, knobs, square keys and indicator lamps. Red appears only for warnings. Motion is typed text, 12fps stepped hardware actions, a brief boot flicker and short channel-static transitions that resolve into readable holds. Avoid continuous strobing, smooth generic easing, pink or purple neon, glassmorphism, gradient blobs and round flat cards.

items.title: Kiteva / 终端双色歌词动画
items.tags: 终端双色歌词动画 Terminal Lyric Duotone Anime Terminal Lyric Duotone Anime: a flat anime music-video grammar in which every composition sits on a CRT-style terminal screen and the subject is read as data. Despite the traditional 'Duotone' name it is a strict three-ink tritone: ultramarine, cream and near-black as hard-edged posterized flat shapes with no gradients, rendered shading or soft airbrush; supplied anime character and scene illustrations appear mostly as held poses staged like cutouts (slow push, rotation, scale, translucent hologram states). Red is a reserved accent for warnings and dark emotional peaks only, used briefly; a whole-frame negative inversion or a short red palette swap may mark one peak. Frame every shot with a mild CRT finish: an oval dark vignette, fine scanlines, seeded grain and thin corner brackets, a §NN section header at top centre and a small audio meter at bottom left. Captions are bilingual monospace lines at the bottom (English above, Chinese below) whose characters resolve from seeded scrambled glyphs into the exact copy with a fine underline that grows like a progress bar; keywords are tinted signal blue (or red at warning beats). One keyword per section may be promoted to a large hero title that enters with a brief RGB-offset split and settles inside a thin elliptical ring. HUD overlays — detection boxes, specimen cards, feature maps, scan percentages, counters — annotate the subject with authored, labelled-illustrative data. Cut to a new composition every few seconds with plain cuts or brief glitch cuts, then hold long enough to read. Avoid gradients, glossy cel shading, neon rainbow palettes, continuous glitching, strobing flashes and illegible microtext.

items.title: Kiteva / 粒子流网络
items.tags: 粒子流网络 Particle Flow Network Particle Flow Network: a stable node-link diagram in which transfer is shown as streams of fine particles travelling along curved connections between circular hubs. Hubs sit in branching clusters around one or a few primary nodes; node size and a soft halo carry importance, and a small set of semantic state accents (active, idle, waiting, fault) mark status alongside text labels. A sparse dotted field and a quiet dark or paper-light surround keep the graph legible. Particle density, direction and speed communicate volume and flow; the layout itself does not drift. Typography is compact and technical: short node names with small secondary metadata in a monospace or neat sans. Applies to knowledge maps, biological pathways, logistics routes, team collaboration and cause-and-effect systems, not only software. Avoid neon rainbow networking clichés, random floating dots with no source or destination, dashboard chrome without a graph, crowded unreadable labels and constant flashing.
